cands.bio: Huntsville native, master plumber, gas fitter and HVAC contractor. He founded Whole Home Solutions in 2019, which employs about eight people. Earlier he worked in restaurant management in New York City. He has not held public office. He was the 2026 Democratic nominee for Alabama's 5th Congressional District.
cands.gaps: Andrew Sneed has never held public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no statements from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, growth and land protection, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school vouchers and teacher pay. His Ballotpedia survey says he wants public schools fully funded and AI regulated, but neither is a position we could match to a specific proposal. The pages we read do not say which organizations endorsed him, other than online voter-guide groups, which we left out. We found no controversies and no foreign ties in the pages we read. Sources conflict on the year he returned to Huntsville (2010 versus 2012).

cands.bio: Republican U.S. representative for Alabama's 5th District since 2023. Born in Monrovia; former firefighter, EMT and 911 dispatcher. Served on the Madison County Commission from 1996 and chaired it from 2012 to 2023. Holds a business degree from Athens State University.

controversies.text: Federal records show $30,000 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $10,845 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; 1 trip paid for by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's affiliate; 1 staff trip paid for by that foundation.
Missed 17 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (2.5%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 4, 2026-03-17 to 2026-03-17.

On October 23, 2020, the Madison County Commission, which Strong chaired, had a Confederate monument moved from the courthouse grounds to a cemetery. The Alabama Attorney General said this broke the state Memorial Preservation Act and sued. A $25,000 fine was paid and the suit was dismissed. County lawyers said an undisclosed third party paid it, not taxpayers.

In November 2019, three Madison County volunteer fire chiefs told WAFF that Strong, the commission chairman and a Monrovia volunteer firefighter, used his influence to favor Monrovia in county budgets. Monrovia led all volunteer stations by over $130,000. Strong said Monrovia pays more property tax and so gets more back. He said he recommends funding but the commission votes on the budget.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump endorsed Strong in the 2026 general election (also in 2022 and 2024).

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Strong on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, school choice or teacher pay. We found no record of his gun-law actions beyond his own statement of support. We also found no sponsored-bill record showing what he did on police pay or on abortion beyond one cosponsored bill. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. His personal-finance disclosures were not reviewed. A campaign-site news headline about a U.S. Chamber endorsement was visible but the article was not, so it is left out.

qual.background: Madison County commissioner from 1996 to 2012 and commission chairman from 2012 to 2023, overseeing a county budget of about $174 million. He has been a U.S. representative since 2023, serving on the Appropriations and Homeland Security committees.
